_readme: Every fact about the practice lives in this file, and only here.

A value written as { "placeholder": ..., "needs": ... } is not known yet. The site shows it as a marked placeholder, and `npm run build:strict` (the publishing workflow) refuses to build while any remain.
To confirm a fact, replace the whole { ... } object with the real value: a string, or a list of strings where the 'needs' text says so.
Run `npm run build` afterwards: it rebuilds the site and regenerates PLACEHOLDERS.md.

url.needs: The public address of the site, ending in a slash. Until it is confirmed, the build uses this repository's GitHub Pages project address.

legalName.needs: The data controller's legal name: the psychologist's own name if they practise as a sole trader, or the registered company name and number.

icoRegistrationNumber.needs: The practice's registration number on the ICO's register of fee payers.

email.needs: The email address clients should write to.

phone.needs: The telephone number clients should call, written as it should appear, e.g. 020 7946 0000.

address.needs: The practice's postal address, as a list of lines.

name.needs: The psychologist's name as it appears on the HCPC register.

title.needs: The psychologist's HCPC protected title, e.g. Clinical Psychologist or Counselling Psychologist.

qualifications.needs: Degrees and professional qualifications, as a list, each with the awarding institution.

hcpcNumber.needs: The HCPC registration number, which for psychologists begins PYL.

bpsMembership.needs: The British Psychological Society membership grade and any divisions, e.g. Chartered Member (CPsychol). Write 'none' if not a member, and the line will be removed.

bio.needs: Two to four short paragraphs, as a list: training, experience and the settings the psychologist has worked in.

photo.needs: A portrait photograph, at least 800 x 1000 pixels, saved in src/assets/img/; write its file name here.

clientGroups.needs: The groups the psychologist sees, e.g. adults, young people, couples, with any age limits.

specialisms.needs: The difficulties the psychologist works with, as a list.

approach.needs: One to three short paragraphs, as a list, in the psychologist's own words: how they work and which therapies they offer.

formats.needs: Whether sessions are online, in person at the practice address, or both, and on which video platform.

appointment.needs: One row per appointment type, e.g. initial assessment; copy the row for each further type.

length.needs: The length of that appointment, e.g. 50 minutes.

fee.needs: The fee for that appointment, in pounds, e.g. £120.

payment.placeholder: How and when fees are paid
payment.needs: Payment methods accepted and when payment is due.

cancellation.needs: How much notice clients must give to cancel or move an appointment, and any charge for late cancellation.

insurers.placeholder: Health insurers the psychologist is registered with
insurers.needs: The insurers with which the psychologist is a registered provider, as a list. Write 'none' if none.

url.needs: The practice's own Calendly scheduling link. Until it is supplied, the site uses Calendly's own demo scheduling page, the one embedded on Calendly's demo site calendly-embed.com, and the booking page says so.

lastUpdated.needs: The date the practice last reviewed and approved the privacy policy, e.g. 3 November 2026.

retention.needs: How long the practice keeps clinical records, booking details, emails and financial records after the last contact.

providers.placeholder: Other services that hold clients' information
providers.needs: Each service that stores clients' information besides Calendly, e.g. email, clinical notes system, video platform, payments, as a list, each with the country where it stores data.

security.placeholder: How records are stored and protected
security.needs: A short description of how clinical records are kept secure, e.g. an encrypted clinical records system and two-factor sign-in.
